name: Factors, multiples, primes, squares & cubes
description: Factors, multiples, primes, square and cube numbers, HCF and LCM.

questions.explanation: 5³ means 5 × 5 × 5 = 125. Multiplying by the index gives 5 × 3 = 15, which is the cube-triple error. Squaring uses only two 5s and gives 25, and writing 53 reads the index as a digit beside the base.

questions.prompt: Find the number below that is not a multiple of 7.
questions.explanation: 49, 98 and 140 are all multiples of 7: 7 × 7, 7 × 14 and 7 × 20. 75 is not, because 7 × 10 = 70 and 7 × 11 = 77. The 7 times table does not stop at 12 × 7, so the multiples carry on past 84.

questions.prompt: Mia writes 3² = 6 and says "you multiply by 2". What has she done?

options.text: Multiplied the base by the index instead of by itself
Added the base and the index

questions.explanation: 3² means 3 × 3 = 9. Mia has done 3 × 2 = 6: the index says how many copies of the base to multiply, not what to multiply the base by. Working out 2³ gives 8, adding gives 5, and the square root of 3 is not a whole number.
29 has no factors other than 1 and itself. 21 = 3 × 7 and 27 = 3 × 9, so they are odd but not prime. 1 is not prime either: a prime has exactly two factors, and 1 has only one.

questions.prompt: Find every product below that is a multiple of 10.
questions.explanation: A product is a multiple of 10 when it contains both a 2 and a 5. 2 × 3 × 5 and 2 × 5 × 7 both do, so both are multiples of 10 — you can see it without working them out. 3 × 5 × 7 has no 2 and 2 × 3 × 7 has no 5, so neither is a multiple of 10.

questions.prompt: Which expression shows 24 as a product of prime factors?
questions.explanation: Every factor in a prime factorisation must itself be prime. 2 × 2 × 2 × 3 uses only primes, and it equals 24. 4 × 6, 2 × 12 and 3 × 8 all equal 24, but none is finished: 4, 6, 12 and 8 are all composite.

questions.prompt: What is the lowest common multiple of 6 and 8?
questions.explanation: Multiples of 6 are 6, 12, 18, 24, … and multiples of 8 are 8, 16, 24, … so the lowest common multiple is 24. Adding 6 + 8 gives 14, which is not a multiple of either. 48 is a common multiple but not the lowest, and 2 is the highest common factor.

questions.prompt: One of these is not a factor of 30. Which one?
questions.explanation: 30 ÷ 5 = 6, 30 ÷ 6 = 5 and 30 ÷ 15 = 2, so 5, 6 and 15 are all factors of 30. 30 ÷ 4 = 7.5, which is not exact, so 4 is not a factor.

questions.prompt: A number has exactly two factors and is greater than 20. Which could it be?
questions.explanation: Exactly two factors means prime. 23 has only 1 and 23. 21 = 3 × 7, 25 = 5 × 5 and 27 = 3 × 9, so each has more than two factors. Being odd is not enough to be prime.

questions.prompt: Which is the complete prime factorisation of 90?
questions.explanation: Keep factorising until every factor is prime. 90 = 2 × 45 = 2 × 3 × 15 = 2 × 3 × 3 × 5, and 2, 3, 3 and 5 are all prime. The other three all equal 90, but each still contains a composite number (15, 9, 10 or 30), so none is complete.

questions.prompt: Is every multiple of 4 also a multiple of 2?
questions.explanation: Always, because 4 = 2 × 2: any number built from 4s is also built from 2s. 4, 8, 12, 16, … are all even. A number such as 6 is a multiple of 2 but not of 4, so not every multiple of 2 is a multiple of 4 — but the question asks the other way round.

questions.prompt: A rectangular path is 24 tiles long and 18 tiles wide. It is covered exactly with the largest possible square tiles. How many tiles along each side of a square tile?
questions.explanation: The side of the tile must divide both 24 and 18, and we want the largest such number: the highest common factor. 24 = 2³ × 3 and 18 = 2 × 3², so the HCF is 2 × 3 = 6. 2 and 3 are common factors but not the highest, and 72 is the lowest common multiple.

questions.prompt: Find the number that is not a square number.
questions.explanation: Square numbers are made by multiplying a whole number by itself: 16 = 4 × 4, 25 = 5 × 5 and 36 = 6 × 6. 12 is not: it lies between 9 and 16, and no whole number multiplied by itself gives 12.

questions.prompt: Three of these are factors of 12. Which one is not?
questions.explanation: The factors of 12 are 1, 2, 3, 4, 6 and 12. 12 ÷ 1, 12 ÷ 3 and 12 ÷ 4 are exact, so those are factors; 12 ÷ 5 = 2.4, so 5 is not.

questions.prompt: A square garden has an area of 49 m². How long is one side?
questions.explanation: The area of a square is side × side, so the side is √49 = 7, because 7 × 7 = 49. A square root is not halving (24.5) or dividing by 3.5 (14). 9 × 9 = 81, which is too big.
